## Episode Thesis

This Norwegian personal-finance episode from VG covers the housing market. August house prices rose 2.1%, which was stronger than expected. Over the past 12 months prices fell in real terms nationally, with big regional gaps: Oslo fell 1% nominally while Tromsø and Bergen each rose about 10%. The host argues that renting now often beats owning over horizons shorter than 3-5 years, especially in Oslo, because professional landlords are selling units and rates are high. He expects Oslo prices to recover in 2027 and says owning remains the right choice long term. Bank rate forecasts are cited, but no equities are discussed in an investment sense.
